claims.disposition: Verified: followed_by_explicit_exact_token_relation matches the 17-verb allowlist L65-86; exact_reference_delimiter_pair lists quoted pairs L157-174 and grouped pairs L175-193. reference_syntax (L49-60) checks delimiter first, then relation. Exact match to the report.

claims.summary: Snag: first_word_after (L89-96) uses split_whitespace + non-alphanumeric trim, so complex punctuation or specific Unicode whitespace 'might fail' to identify the relation verb.
claims.disposition: Concern preserved; source contradicts the failure mode for the named cases. split_whitespace splits on Unicode White_Space; trim_matches(!alnum && !'_') collapses all-punctuation chunks and find(!is_empty) skips them to the next word. Punctuation/soft-hyphen/NBSP/double-dash edge cases isolate the verb; an internal format char fails closed (marker stripped, safe), never leaks. Grounded by passing tests below.

claims.summary: Snag: longest_exact_known_model_control_marker_at (L97) max_by_key(len) must be 'perfectly tuned' to avoid greedy misidentification if a new marker is a substring of another.
claims.disposition: Verified: max_by_key(token.len) over prefix-matching markers is correct maximal-munch; two distinct equal-length strings cannot both prefix one tail, so no tie. No current marker is a prefix of another (checked all 20 in fallback_contracts.rs L159-180), so the concern is forward-looking; longest-overlapping-token test already proves the longest wins.
